topic: The Panama Canal runs on rain (60-second sample)
method: Panama Canal Authority advisory (primary), Library of Congress photographs (primary), Wikipedia and Britannica cross-checks; the pool comparison is computed.

claims.claim: The Panama Canal opened on 15 August 1914; the S.S. Ancon made the opening transit.

sources.title: Library of Congress, 'Opening of the Panama Canal. S.S. Ancon entering east chamber of Pedro Miguel locks', 1914 Aug. 15
sources.quote: Opening of the Panama Canal. S.S. Ancon entering east chamber of Pedro Miguel locks. 1914 Aug. 15

claims.claim: The canal is 82 km long and links the Caribbean Sea to the Pacific Ocean.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Panama Canal' (read 13 Nov 2026)
sources.quote: Length 82 km (51 miles) ... Start point Caribbean Sea ... End point Pacific Ocean

sources.title: Panama Canal Authority, 'Panama Canal to increase daily transits to 24 starting in January', 15 Dec 2023 (Advisory to Shipping A-54-2023)

claims.claim: Locks at each end lift ships up to Gatun Lake, an artificial fresh-water lake 26 metres above sea level, then lower them at the other end.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Panama Canal' (read 13 Nov 2026)
sources.quote: Locks at each end lift ships up to Gatun Lake, an artificial fresh water lake 26 meters (85 ft) above sea level

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Panama Canal: Locks'
sources.quote: locks raise ships to Gatun Lake

claims.claim: Each ship's passage uses about 200 million litres (52 million US gallons) of fresh water.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Panama Canal' (read 13 Nov 2026)
sources.quote: For each ship that passes through, about 200 million liters (52 million gallons) of freshwater are needed.

sources.title: WaterWorld, 'Leveraging data to optimize shipping through the Panama Canal while protecting local water supply'
sources.quote: about 50 million gallons of fresh water per transit

contradictions: An average; it varies with the locks and the ship.

claims.claim: 200 million litres is about 80 Olympic-size pools (2,500 cubic metres, i.e. 2.5 million litres, each). Computed.

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Olympic-size swimming pool' (50 m x 25 m x 2 m minimum depth = 2,500 cubic metres)
sources.quote: 50 m long, 25 m wide, at least 2 m deep: 2,500 m3

contradictions: Computed from the average transit volume.

claims.claim: October 2023 was the driest October on record for the Canal Watershed.

sources.title: Panama Canal Authority, 'Panama Canal to increase daily transits to 24 starting in January', 15 Dec 2023 (Advisory to Shipping A-54-2023)
sources.quote: October 2023 marked the driest October on record for the Canal Watershed.

claims.claim: Normally 36 ships transit each day; in December 2023 the canal allowed 22; from January 2024, 24.

sources.title: Panama Canal Authority, 'Panama Canal to increase daily transits to 24 starting in January', 15 Dec 2023 (Advisory to Shipping A-54-2023)
sources.quote: TOTAL 36 22 24 (Regular Scenario, Current Period, January 2024) ... Currently, 22 vessels transit daily

sources.title: Wikipedia, 'Panama Canal' (read 13 Nov 2026)
sources.quote: In normal times, 36 ships can transit the canal each day, but in early December 2023 ... only 22 ships per day ... In January 2024, 24 ships per day

claims.claim: The Panama Canal Authority said 2023 marked the first time the canal had ever had to restrict transits.

sources.title: Panama Canal Authority, 'Panama Canal to increase daily transits to 24 starting in January', 15 Dec 2023 (Advisory to Shipping A-54-2023)
sources.quote: This year marks the first time the Canal has ever had to restrict transits.
